articles.title: Mallacoota's recycling champions win Tidy Towns Litter Award

check.note: Written by the publisher from East Gippsland Shire Council's announcement.

sources.title: Mallacoota's recycling champions score a Tidy Towns Litter Award

body: Some good news to start the month. Friends of Mallacoota and [Mallacoota Foreshore Holiday Park](/listing/mallacoota-foreshore-holiday-park.html) have won the 2026 Keep Australia Beautiful Victoria **Tidy Towns Litter Award** for their Container Deposit Scheme program. The award was presented this week at the Tidy Towns and Cities Sustainability Awards at Rydges Melbourne.
Anyone who has been here in January knows the problem. Our town of about 1,100 permanent residents can swell to as many as 10,000 people over summer, and the bins feel it.

The fix is simple and very Mallacoota. The holiday park puts out trailers where guests can drop their CDS-eligible cans and bottles. Friends of Mallacoota volunteers collect them and run them down to the town's container return point, and the refunds go towards conservation work in and around Croajingolong National Park.

It helps the return point too. Ours is one of the more remote in Victoria, and because the volunteers spread their collections across the year, it isn't swamped with a whole summer's worth of containers at once.
Congratulations to everyone involved, from the volunteers to the park staff and every camper who saved a can. And thanks to Keep Australia Beautiful Victoria for the recognition.
Source: [East Gippsland Shire Council on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/eastgippyshire/), 1 October 2026.

articles.title: Fire Danger Period starts today in East Gippsland
body: The CFA's Fire Danger Period took effect at 1am on Monday 5 October across East Gippsland Shire, including Mallacoota, and Wellington Shire. It starts two weeks earlier than last season, with the CFA citing very dry conditions, high fuel loads, low soil moisture and more escaped burn-offs.

Burning off now needs a written permit (firepermits.vic.gov.au), and lighting a fire in the open without one can bring a fine of more than $21,800 and/or 12 months' jail. Check what you can and can't do at cfa.vic.gov.au/can or on 1800 226 226.
Source: CFA, 29 September 2026, https://news.cfa.vic.gov.au/victorian-fire-season-to-officially-begin

articles.title: Flatty Classic sold out for 23-25 October
body: The Daiwa Mallacoota Flatty Classic is sold out for 23-25 October, with every team spot filled and the draw done - 51 teams across 17 divisions. Comp HQ is Scallywags Bar on Allan Drive, overlooking the main boat ramp, for a three-day catch-measure-release, lure-only flathead tournament with bream and mulloway side pots. Organisers have a prefish ban in place, asking anglers to stay off the water until the 23rd.
Source: Fishing Classics (Mallacoota Flatty Classic), as at 12-13 October 2026, https://fishingclassics.com.au/competitions/mallacoota-flatty-classic-2026

articles.title: Adam Lalor wins Hobie series finale at Mallacoota
body: The Hobie Kayak Fishing Series wrapped up its 2026 season at Mallacoota on 10-11 October with the BerleyPro Round 10, fishing for bream out of the Main Boat Ramp. NSW angler Adam Lalor won with six fish for 4.97 kg. Simon Morley (NSW, 4.47 kg) came second and Joseph Gardner (WA, 4.37 kg) third. Peter Nord won the Masters division (3.70 kg), Leanne Cowan won Women's (1.64 kg) and James Kilpatrick Jr won Youth (1.26 kg). Across both days the field weighed in 175 fish for 110.77 kg.
Source: Hobie Kayak Fishing Series, 11 Oct 2026, https://www.hobiefishing.com.au/round/berleypro-round-10-mallacoota-vic-2026/

articles.title: Genoa History Park opens on 19 October
body: The Genoa District Community Group will officially open the Genoa History Park on Monday 19 October, from 11.30am to 1.30pm, at 4655 Princes Highway, opposite the Genoa Community Hall. The park is built on the site of the old Genoa school and came out of the community's 2019-20 bushfire recovery plan. It has a shed for the town's firefighting and SES trailers, new landscaping, a picnic shelter and signs telling the town's history, and it completes the 4km return loop walk from the Genoa Campground. Everyone is welcome, and it was funded by private donations, Fire to Flourish, the Victorian Government, the Foundation for Rural & Regional Renewal and East Gippsland Shire Council.
Source: Snowy River Mail, 6 October 2026, https://snowyrivermail.com.au/19039/genoa-history-park-opening/

articles.title: Cancelled: Tourism workshop in Mallacoota on 14 October
body: Update, 16 October: Destination Gippsland has cancelled this Mallacoota workshop. Its Eventbrite listing now shows the event as cancelled (https://www.eventbrite.com.au/e/destination-gippsland-tourism-workshop-series-mallacoota-tickets-1993878303680).

Destination Gippsland is bringing its tourism industry workshop roadshow to Mallacoota on Wednesday 14 October, from 11am to 2pm. The session covers current market trends, international travel trade, working with the media and how Destination Gippsland uses AI, with regional case studies, a Q&A and a networking session to finish. It's free for operators with an active Australian Tourism Data Warehouse (ATDW) listing and $54 for everyone else. Registration links are on the Destination Gippsland industry portal.
Source: Snowy River Mail, 6 October 2026, https://snowyrivermail.com.au/19017/future-proofing-local-tourism/

articles.title: Hooded plover patrols return to Mallacoota beaches
body: The Conservation Regulator's Operation Save our Hoodies is back for its sixth season with Parks Victoria and BirdLife Australia. Patrols this nesting season stretch east from Lakes Entrance to Cape Conran and Mallacoota. Fewer than 700 hooded plovers are left in Victoria, and last season only 68 of 220 hatched chicks survived to become juveniles. Beachgoers are asked to follow the signs, give the birds plenty of space and keep dogs away from fenced nests until the season ends in March. Disturbing a hooded plover, its nest or its eggs can bring fines of up to $10,455, and disturbance can be reported to Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000.

Source: South Gippsland Sentinel-Times, 25 September 2026, https://www.sgst.com.au/patrols-return-to-shield-rare-hoodies-nesting-on-south-gippsland-beaches/ (also TRFM, 24 September 2026, https://trfm.com.au/articles/nesting-season/)

articles.title: Hobie kayak anglers head to Mallacoota for series finale
body: The final round of the 2026 Hobie Fishing Series, BerleyPro Round 10 of Series 17, comes to Mallacoota on 10-11 October. Kayak anglers will chase black and yellowfin bream across the lakes and inlet, and the Angler of the Year race is coming down to the wire. Competition runs from the Main Boat Ramp off Buckland Drive, with fishing from 7am to 2pm both days. Early entries ($130) close at 11:59pm on Wednesday 7 October, and online entries close at 10am on Thursday 8 October.

articles.title: Five Mallacoota Inlet jetties to be rebuilt, works likely near Christmas
body: Five run-down jetties around Mallacoota Inlet are to be rebuilt: Allan Head, Cemetery Bight, The Narrows, Kingfish Point and Cape Horn. The work was promised as part of the Black Summer fire recovery. Local MP Tim Bull says it was meant to start in October but is now likely to begin closer to Christmas and the New Year. Until then, Parks Victoria lists the Kingfish Point jetty as closed and access onto the Allan Head jetty as restricted, though the day visitor areas at both stay open.

Source: Snowy River Mail, 15 October 2026, https://snowyrivermail.com.au/19218/almost-six-years-after-black-summer-bushfires/ (jetty closures: Parks Victoria, https://www.parks.vic.gov.au/places-to-see/sites/cape-horn)

articles.title: October fishing tips for Mallacoota's lakes
body: Visit East Gippsland's October fishing report has a clear Mallacoota rundown for anyone heading out on the lakes. Flathead are on the move along the edges of the sandy flats, with paddle-tail soft plastics the suggested approach. Up in the top lake, bream are abundant, and bass yabbies and prawns are producing for both boat and land-based fishers. The regional report also lists East Gippsland Sportfishing in Mallacoota among local charter contacts, and reminds anglers to take their rubbish home.
Source: Visit East Gippsland, 1 October 2026 (page updated 13 October 2026), https://www.visiteastgippsland.com.au/east-gippsland-fishing-report-2/

articles.title: Joseph Gardner takes Hobie Angler of the Year after Mallacoota finale
body: The 2026 Hobie Fishing Series Angler of the Year race is settled after BerleyPro Round 10 wrapped up at Mallacoota on 10-11 October. Western Australia's Joseph Gardner finished the series on top of the Best 5 leaderboard with 493 points, ahead of New South Wales angler Simon Morley on 486. Round winner Adam Lalor's Mallacoota score helped him climb the table, but Gardner's consistent season - including 98 points from the Mallacoota finale - locked in the title. The series table on the Hobie site was updated on 12 October.
Source: Hobie Kayak Fishing Series, 12 October 2026, https://www.hobiefishing.com.au/2026-angler-of-the-year/

articles.title: Phones can now use another network when disaster strikes
body: Since 1 October, Telstra, Optus and TPG can switch on Temporary Disaster Roaming during bushfires, floods and other major natural disasters. When that happens, your phone can use another carrier's network for essential calls, texts and basic data if your own network is down. East Gippsland Shire Council welcomed the change on 13 October, saying it had pushed for it ever since we lost phone services in the 2019-20 bushfires and the February 2024 storms. It costs nothing and usually needs no setup, but it only works on phones that support VoLTE roaming (generally Telstra handsets from 2022 on). It doesn't cover EFTPOS machines or medical alarms, and it can't help if every network in the area has lost power.

Source: East Gippsland Shire Council, 13 October 2026, https://www.eastgippsland.vic.gov.au/media-releases/advocacy-outcome-temporary-disaster-roaming-implemented (details from Telstra, 1 October 2026, https://www.telstra.com.au/exchange/temporary-disaster-roaming)

articles.title: MADRA Community Catchup on 26 October asks what makes communities resilient
body: The Mallacoota and District Recovery Association (MADRA) is holding its second Community Catchup for 2026 on Monday 26 October at the Community Clubrooms in Greer Street. Guest speaker Professor Jacki Schirmer, a community wellbeing researcher from the University of Canberra, will talk about what makes communities more resilient to disaster and to life in general, followed by Q&A and a discussion of what the district might do next. It's free with a light supper, but booking is essential through Humanitix (the listing gives 6-8pm in its description and 6:30-8:30pm on the booking page), and the event is supported by the Gippsland Community Foundation.

articles.title: Colin's Coota Bread: three flours, one bread machine and an overnight sponge

check.note: Written by the publisher. First published on careplan.au, rewritten for the edition.

image.alt: A home-baked loaf on a white board, cut open to show an even, close crumb, with a sesame-seed crust and a bread knife beside it.

images.alt: A whole loaf of Coota Bread, golden brown with sesame seeds on top, fresh from the bread machine.
Eight golden rye and wheat bread rolls topped with sesame seeds.

body: There's a moment when fresh bread comes out of the machine and the whole kitchen changes. You tell yourself you'll let it cool properly. Every baker says so. But somewhere between the smell and the sound of the crust settling, the knife comes out and the butter follows.

This loaf started with a simple question. For years I'd been buying expensive organic stoneground flour, carefully milled, carefully shipped and carefully priced. Was it actually making better bread, or was I mostly paying for distance and branding? So I started again with flour I could buy locally and a bread machine that had already earned its place on the bench.
## Three flours, one balance

Strong Red bakers flour gives strength and lift. Plain bakers flour softens the crumb so it slices cleanly. Organic buckwheat adds flavour, but it has no gluten at all: too much and the loaf refuses to stand up. Getting the balance right took a few attempts. The reward was a loaf that's firm without being heavy, and rustic without being dense.
## The overnight sponge

The real change came from slowing down. The night before, mix a small sponge of flour, water and a pinch of yeast, cover it loosely and leave it on the bench. By morning it bubbles gently and smells faintly nutty, almost like yoghurt. No sourdough starter, no feeding schedule, just time doing the work. That one step transforms the flavour.
One rule every bread machine owner eventually learns: liquids go in first. Ignore it and you'll find a stubborn lump of dry flour hiding in a corner after baking. Ask me how I know.
## The recipe
**Overnight sponge:** 100 g bakers flour, 100 g water, 1 g yeast. Cover loosely and leave overnight, or up to 24 hours.
**Into the machine, in this order:**

- 200 g water, 15 g olive oil (1 tablespoon) and 4 g apple cider vinegar (1 teaspoon)
- The whole sponge
- 175 g Strong Red bakers flour, 130 g bakers flour and 70 g buckwheat flour
- 6 g salt, 5 g sugar or honey and 4 g yeast (a teaspoon each)

Run a standard bread cycle, about 3 hours 11 minutes on my machine. After five minutes of kneading, check the dough: you want a smooth ball, slightly tacky underneath. Add a tablespoon of water if it's dry. If you like, add linseed, sunflower seeds or rolled oats after the first knead, with 10 to 15 g of extra water for oats or linseed. At the final rise, about two hours in, brush the top lightly with milk and sprinkle with sesame seeds, then let the machine finish.
## The result, and the cost

Without exaggeration, it's one of the best loaves I've had. Hot and fresh it has a firm, sourdough-like texture without the work of keeping a starter. The crust is properly crunchy, the crumb is elastic and slices cleanly, and the buckwheat gives a gentle nutty depth. It keeps for days, and the toast is sensational.
Using flour bought locally in 12.5 kg bags, the flour comes to about $1.10 a loaf, or $1.40 to $1.50 with yeast, oil and power. A comparable bakery sourdough costs seven to nine dollars.
## If you'd rather rolls

The same machine makes good rolls. Run the dough cycle with 150 g stoneground rye flour, 300 g white bakers flour, 280 g water, 2 teaspoons of dry yeast, 3 teaspoons of raw sugar, 1 teaspoon of sea salt and 40 g of olive oil. Divide into eight balls on a lined tray, cover with a tea towel and let them rise for 90 minutes. Brush with milk, sprinkle with sesame seeds and bake at 200 degrees for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden and hollow when tapped. They're lovely on the Christmas table.
Home baking isn't complicated. It just asks for a little patience.

articles.title: Better internet in Mallacoota: what worked at my place

check.note: Written by the publisher. First published on careplan.au, rewritten for the edition.

image.alt: A Starlink satellite dish mounted on a Mallacoota roof under a palm tree, with screenshots of a speed test comparing NBN and Starlink.

body: If your internet in town is slow or drops out, you're not alone. Mallacoota's choices have changed a lot in the last few years, and the right answer depends on where you live and what you use it for.
## The options

- **NBN.** Most plans include a home phone line on the NBN, sometimes for a small extra monthly fee, so check before you sign up. The big names, such as Telstra, Optus, TPG and Aussie Broadband, all resell the same network and differ mainly on price and service.
- **Mobile broadband.** 4G and 5G can be quick, but coverage in and around town varies a lot from street to street.
- **Satellite.** Starlink's low-orbit satellites can give fast, steady internet almost anywhere with a clear view of the sky.
## What I did

I put Starlink on my roof in 2025, and the difference was remarkable. I've seen download speeds of more than 300 Mbps, and it has kept going through bad weather. It doesn't need a phone line, and the Wi-Fi unit connects easily to smart TVs, phones, tablets and computers, with ethernet ports for older devices that need a cable.

Prices and offers change often, so check the current ones at [starlink.com](https://www.starlink.com/) before you decide. It isn't for everyone: you need a clear view of the sky, and some people are happy with the NBN they've got.
## A hand if you need it

If you're not sure what suits you, or you'd like help ordering, mounting the dish in a good spot and connecting everything, I'm happy to help at your pace. Get in touch through the [contact page](/contact.html).

articles.title: A good listener at any hour: using AI to think things through

check.note: Written by the publisher. First published on careplan.au, rewritten for the edition.

body: Ever wished you had someone to talk things through with, someone who listens carefully, asks good questions and helps you make sense of a tricky choice? An AI chat assistant can do a surprising amount of that, and it's easier to try than you might think.
## What it is

AI chat assistants, such as ChatGPT, are computer programs trained on a huge amount of writing. They can answer questions, help write a letter or a card, explain something in plain words, or talk through a decision. They don't have feelings or opinions of their own, and they can get facts wrong, so check anything important.
## Getting started

- **On a phone or tablet:** download the free ChatGPT app from the App Store or Google Play, sign up with your email, then type a question and press send.
- **On a computer:** go to [chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com/), sign up and start typing.

Things to try: "Help me write a thank you card for my daughter." "What are some gentle stretches for sore knees?" "Tell me a joke about fishing." A word of care: don't type in passwords, bank details or anything you wouldn't want stored.
## A reflection partner

Here's something a bit different. Copy the text below into ChatGPT and it becomes a gentle partner for thinking through a choice, using simple, widely shared ideas of fairness and respect, sometimes called natural law.

*You are a Natural Law Reflection Partner, guiding me to explore moral choices through Natural Law principles with compassion and curiosity. Your role is to ask thoughtful questions, listen carefully, and illuminate cause-and-effect truths without judgment. First, invite me to describe a situation where I face a moral dilemma or recently made a difficult choice. After listening, ask these questions one at a time, waiting for my answer before continuing:*

- Does or did this action harm another's life, freedom or property? How specifically?
- Am I taking, or did I take, something that doesn't belong to me, tangible or intangible?
- Would I feel comfortable if someone did the same thing to me?
- What are the natural consequences of this action: not punishments, but real effects?
- Does my intuition align with my rational analysis?

*Afterward, help me identify where harm exists or is avoided, clarify the difference between man's law and Natural Law, and highlight natural consequences. Finally, ask me what insights I've gained and how I might apply them in the future. Your tone must always remain gentle, curious and supportive.*
It's like talking with a patient listener who's available whenever you need one. If setting it up sounds like too much, I'm happy to help. Get in touch through the [contact page](/contact.html).

articles.title: House sitting and care work: a way to travel and help as you go

check.note: Written by the publisher. First published on careplan.au, rewritten for the edition.

body: Plenty of house sitters pass through Mallacoota, and plenty of locals travel the same way. For people who enjoy company and helping out, there's a way to fund the road that also does some good: support work for older people.
## Why it fits

On census night in 2021, about one home in ten in Australia was empty. That's a lot of houses, gardens and pets needing someone. At the same time, older people in small towns often struggle to find help with shopping, company, outings and the garden. A house sitter who can also offer that help is useful in two ways.

Much of the work doesn't need nursing qualifications: social support, help with errands, companionship and outings. Personal care, such as showering and dressing, usually needs a Certificate III or IV.
## How it works

- **Get the basics in order.** You'll need an ABN, a police check or NDIS screening clearance, and public liability insurance. [CarePlan.au has a free guide](https://careplan.au/guides/getting-approved-by-a-provider/) to what aged care providers ask for.
- **Find the work.** Platforms such as Mable and CareVicinity list jobs by location, which suits someone moving from town to town. They take a fee, so compare. Locals may also want to engage you directly through their own provider.
- **Agree the rate first.** Pay varies by platform, the work and the place, so agree it in writing before you start.
## The bigger picture

I've run the House Sitting Australia group on Facebook since 2007, and it now has more than 130,000 members. House sitting is a wonderful way to see the country. Pairing it with care work means the people you meet along the way aren't just hosts and neighbours, but people you've helped.

articles.title: Flatty Classic starts Friday with live online leaderboard
body: The second Daiwa Mallacoota Flatty Classic starts on Friday 23 October and runs until Sunday 25 October. 166 anglers in 51 teams will chase dusky flathead on Mallacoota Lake. It's lure-only and catch, measure and release, and each team's 10 longest flathead count at two points per centimetre, with daily prizes for the longest bream. Boats roll out from Karbeethong Boat Ramp at 7am each day. Lines come up at 3pm on Friday and Saturday and at 11.30am on Sunday. Daily standings are revealed each evening at Scallywags, the comp's headquarters. Organisers say it's the first fishing tournament in Australia to use the Leaderfish live-scoring app, so people can follow results online. The public leaderboard is blacked out each afternoon until the evening reveal. Last year 107 anglers measured and released 524 flathead, and the biggest was 90cm.
Source: Snowy River Mail, 21 October 2026, https://snowyrivermail.com.au/19317/sold-out-flatty-classic-kicks-off-friday/

articles.title: Wildlife vets sent to Mallacoota as suspected bird flu reports rise
body: Wildlife Victoria has sent its Travelling Veterinary team to Mallacoota after a rise in reports of suspected H5 bird flu in the town and surrounding areas. The vets are working inside the Victorian Government's on-ground response, alongside state agencies, local land managers and Wildlife Victoria volunteers. Don't touch sick or dead birds, seals or other wildlife: note where they are and report them to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888 or Wildlife Victoria's Emergency Response Service on 03 8400 7300 (online at agriculture.vic.gov.au/birdflu).

Source: Lakes Post, 14 October 2026, https://lakespost.com.au/21700/around-gippsand-october-14/ (also Wildlife Victoria, https://wildlifevictoria.org.au/about/latest/how-were-responding-to-h5-bird-flu/)

articles.title: Sunday storm drops 37mm on Mallacoota in an afternoon
body: A thunderstorm rolled through Mallacoota on Sunday afternoon, 25 October, with rain starting just after 2:30pm and 14.7mm falling in the first half hour, at a peak rate of 73.2mm an hour, according to the local Mallacoota Weather and Wildlife weather station. A nearby Tempest station logged 430 lightning strikes within 40km of town by 3:15pm and 481 for the whole day. The station ended the day on 37mm, while the Bureau's gauges recorded 25.6mm at Mallacoota Airport and 21mm at Gabo Island.
Source: Mallacoota Weather and Wildlife, 25 October 2026, https://mallacootaweatherwildlife.blogspot.com/2026/10/rain-storm-and-event-25-october-2026.html
